Tessa —

Thanks for the doc. Attached is the ACME edge diagram you requested (acme-edge-diagram.pdf). A couple of clarifying questions from security and SRE after a quick review: 

1) We need a clearer statement on where log/telemetry egress originates. Will telemetry exit from Redwood-managed NAT IPs in our colo or from the tenant-facing runtime nodes?
2) Are you proposing any inbound firewall rules to allow Redwood control-plane heartbeats, or will that be entirely tunneled over an outbound connection initiated from our side?
3) Can you provide expected expected BGP sessions / ASN and whether the connection requires our side to peer with a dedicated leaf or a shared fabric?

We are available Thu 09:00-11:00 PT for a short call.

Thanks —
Eric

Subject: Fwd: On-prem VPC attachment snapshot + demarcation risks (internal)

Team —

Pasting Eric's questions from ACME. We should align on short answers we can give on Thursday's call. I propose the following drafts: 

- Telemetry egress: default behavior will be telemetry initiated from runtime nodes to our telemetry endpoints (Redwood-managed). For private deployments we can optionally route telemetry via a customer NAT (ACME-managed) — that option adds configuration steps (see risk #2 in demarcation-risks-notes.txt).
- Control-plane reachability: control-plane uses an outbound TLS tunnel initiated from the control-plane agents inside the customer VPC. No inbound trust is required on their firewall for heartbeats; only the egress rules must allow TLS to our control endpoints.
- BGP/peering: we support both direct BGP and static routes. For performance and predictability we recommend a dedicated leaf with a /30 and an explicit ASN for the session — but we can accept a shared fabric if ACME cannot allocate a dedicated leaf.

Action items before call: 
1) Kimberly — confirm the exact IP ranges and ports we recommend for egress in the public doc (I left placeholders in the PDF).
2) Aditya — prepare a short talking script on how we handle KV-cache and data-plane pinning to tenant runtime nodes (1 slide).
3) Marissa — I'll need you on the call to capture procurement windows and any contract-level blocking items.

If you all agree, I'll send a calendar invite for Thu 09:30 PT.

Tessa

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: On-prem VPC attachment snapshot + demarcation risks (internal)

Tessa/Team —

I've updated the egress section and attached a short checklist for the call (runbook-egress-checklist.xlsx). Key notes: 
- Egress IPs: 34.198.12.0/28 (TLS endpoints) and 34.198.12.32/28 (metrics/telemetry). Recommend allowing outbound TCP 443 and UDP 123 if time sync via NTP is required in your environment.
- Control-plane: outbound TLS only; heartbeats over persistent TLS. No inbound ports required on customer firewall.
- BGP: recommend dedicated ASN + /30. If ACME cannot provide a dedicated leaf, we will fall back to route-based adjacency over the shared fabric and use NAT for node egress.

I've flagged risk item #3 in the original notes (procurement window) — if procurement blocks cross-connects for >6 weeks we'll propose a staged approach: initial attachment via IPsec tunnels (temporary) then cutover to direct cross-connect once provisioning completes.

Kimberly Park
NetOps 
Redwood Inference

Eric —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the ACME edge diagram. Per our internal alignment (see notes below) we think the clean path forward for Thursday's call is: 

1) Confirm egress ACLs (we propose the two /28 ranges below to keep it tight).
2) Confirm you can accept outbound TLS-only control-plane (no inbound ports to your border required).
3) Decide on the BGP option: dedicated leaf preferred; fallback is NAT/shared fabric.

If those look good, we'll walk the updated PDF on the call and mark acceptance criteria. Attaching the runbook checklist to the invite.
